primary_claim: The introspection effect observed when steering vectors are injected into small open-weight LLMs (the model saying 'Yes' to having detected an injected thought) is mainly attributable to steering-induced confusion/noise rather than genuine introspection.
contradicts_or_qualifies: Anthropic's 'Emergent Introspective Awareness in Large Language Models' paper claiming LLMs can introspect on injected activations
stated_future_work: If genuine introspection does exist in larger models, it would be fascinating to study how it emerges with scale and to understand its mechanistic underpinnings.
A more systematic treatment of control questions is needed to rule out the effect being pure noise.
limitations_stated: Experiments have no bearing on larger models.
Only tested small open-weight models on hardware the author could run comfortably.
quote: The main takeaway is that the introspection effect (that the LLM appears to detect an injected thought) is present in small LLMs but mainly attributable to "confusion" or noise
